newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn's extra budget violates constitution - expert.
newsitem.headline: Bonn's extra budget violates constitution - expert.

text.p: A key adviser to the German government was quoted on Thursday as saying he believed Finance Minister Theo Waigel's supplementary budget for 1997 violated the constitution.
The supplementary budget means Germany's deficit would be higher than investment -- something the constitution forbids unless parliament declares a situation of economic imbalance.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition plans to use this proviso to pass the supplementary budget, arguing that high unemployment of over four million constitutes an imbalance.

But Rolf Peffekoven, a member of the Council of Economic Advisers dubbed Germany's "Five Wise Men," said there was no evidence Waigel was using the higher deficit to cut unemployment, according to the Tagesspiegel newspaper, in an advance release from Friday's edition.
"For this reason, I view the planned higher use of credit as not conforming to the constitution," the paper quoted him as saying.
